setlist.title: I've Been All Around This World

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Bird Song** (2 reviews): Singled out as a highlight of the acoustic set; Described as soothing [12][14]
- **Dire Wolf** (1 review): Opens the acoustic set strongly [14]
- **Monkey And The Engineer** (1 review): Reviewer enjoyed hearing this one in the acoustic set [18]
- **Jack-A-Roe** (1 review): Reviewer found it a really nice moment in the acoustic set [18]
- **China Doll** (1 review): Reviewer says it stands out in the set [14]
- **Ripple** (1 review): Jerry urges the audience to sing along as the song starts [10]
- **The Music Never Stopped** (1 review): Reviewer suggests skipping straight to this song for a quick dose of the band's magic [13]
- **Brokedown Palace** (1 other source): Listed as the encore [1]

## The recordings

- **gd80-10-03.nak300.vernon.16208.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 30 songs; 188 min; rated 3/5 by 5 [1]
- **gd1980-10-03.nak700.ellner.koucky.89128.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 30 songs; 190 min; rated 4/5 by 5 [2]. Said about its sound: A small blip occurs at 1:17 in The Wheel on disc 3, track 6 [2]
- **gd1980-10-03.165795.sbd.tape1.1gen.miller.t-flac1644**: soundboard; 14 songs; 79 min [3]
- **gd1980-10-03.acoustic.mtx.seamons.94131.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 10 songs; 48 min; rated 4/5 by 5 [6]

## Around the show

- Reviewer says they attended all the weekend shows at this venue [8]
- Weir tells off a howler in the crowd, noting Jerry wrote the song for his mother [10]
- Ron Ellner recorded and archived it to reels; the master cassettes were stolen [6]
- Reviewer rates the acoustic set on the 11th as the best of the run [8]
- Recommends this show to anyone who likes the album Reckoning [9]
- Reviewer says the high-energy electric set stands up well against 1977 shows [11]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd80-10-03.nak300.vernon.16208.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience Recording: Nak 300 [1]. Also: Nak300 to Sony TC-152 to AMC to CoolEdit Pro to CD, via Charles Gannon, encoded by Matt Vernon [1]
- **gd1980-10-03.nak700.ellner.koucky.89128.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Ron Ellner; transferred by Bill Koucky; source: Master Cassette > Nakamichi 700’s > Sony TC D-5 > Teak Reel to Reel [2]. Also: Crossfades were applied during tape flips and pauses between tunes [2]
- **gd1980-10-03.165795.sbd.tape1.1gen.miller.t-flac1644**: transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  February 9, 2023; source: SBD > Cassette Master (Nakamichi 550) > Cassette (Sony TC-D5M/TDK SA-C90) [3]. Also: Pitch was confirmed with help from Joe B. Jones; First-generation soundboard tape, converted from 24/96 to 16/44 format [3]
- **gd1980-10-03.acoustic.mtx.seamons.94131.flac16**: transferred by Hunter Seamons; source: Matrix mix (SBD/AUD) [6]. Also: Master cassette recorded on Nakamichi 700s to Sony TC D-5, taped from front of board, on floor or first-row balcony; Mike Marino transferred the reels to PC; seed came via David Gans, Chris Meyer and Charlie Miller [6]
